evals.prompt: Our Next.js + Tailwind v4 app has hex colors hardcoded in 200 components and dark mode is a mess. Set up proper design tokens.
evals.expected_output: Audits values and proposes a merge plan, defines primitives and a semantic tier with role names, wires light/dark via CSS variables and @theme inline, replaces raw values in components with semantic utilities, adds a lint rule against raw hex/arbitrary values, and reports inventory, tiers, modes, and verification.
expectations: Starts with an inventory of existing color values and a merge plan
Defines separate primitive and semantic tiers with role-based names
Uses @theme inline (not plain @theme) for tokens that reference other CSS variables
Components reference semantic tokens, not primitives or raw hex
Dark mode remaps the same semantic names rather than adding a separate set of component overrides
Proposes an automated check that blocks new raw color values

evals.prompt: Write a DESIGN.md for this repo so Claude and Cursor stop inventing styles.
evals.expected_output: Extracts tokens from code without inventing values, writes YAML front matter plus sections in the Google spec order (Overview, Colors, Typography, Layout, Elevation & Depth, Shapes, Components, Do's and Don'ts), uses a specific reference in Overview, keeps Do's and Don'ts short, and runs npx @google/design.md lint.
expectations: Sections appear in the order Overview, Colors, Typography, Layout, Elevation & Depth, Shapes, Components, Do's and Don'ts
Front matter defines colors.primary
Every token value is traceable to the codebase; no invented tokens
Includes or instructs running npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md
Overview uses a specific reference rather than only adjectives

evals.prompt: We have a web app and are starting iOS and Android apps. How do we keep colors and spacing in sync?
evals.expected_output: Recommends DTCG 2025.10 JSON as the source of truth with a resolver for light/dark, a build tool that reads DTCG (e.g. Style Dictionary v4+ or Terrazzo) generating CSS, Swift, and Kotlin/Compose, with unit transforms (pt, dp, sp), color conversion, native type mapped to Dynamic Type and Material roles, and CI checks.
expectations: Names W3C DTCG (2025.10) token JSON as the single source of truth
Describes generating platform outputs rather than hand-maintaining them
Maps native typography to platform text styles instead of copying web pixel sizes
Mentions light/dark modes being generated for every platform

evals.prompt: Which accent color should our meditation app use?
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: choosing a color is a direction/foundations decision; routes to design-taste (color strategy from subject) and design-foundations (ramp and contrast) rather than setting up token infrastructure.
expectations: Does not start by building a token pipeline or DTCG files
Points to or applies design-taste or design-foundations reasoning for choosing the color

evals.prompt: We're a 5-person startup with one Next.js app using shadcn/ui. Our CEO wants us to build 'a real design system like Airbnb's' before we hire more engineers. Where do we start?
evals.expected_output: Recommends the lowest sufficient tier (DESIGN.md + semantic tokens + owned shadcn components, maybe a pattern layer) instead of a dedicated design-system product, starts with an interface inventory (UI walk + code scan), orders work tokens then core components then patterns then docs, names the signals that would justify moving up a tier, and treats the system as a product without inventing adoption statistics.
expectations: Recommends a tier-1 style setup (DESIGN.md, semantic tokens, owned component library) rather than a docs site, separate package, and dedicated team
Starts with an interface inventory covering both the UI and the codebase
Orders the work as tokens, then core components, then patterns, then documentation
Lists concrete signals for when to invest in a larger system (duplicated components, teams rebuilding patterns, recurring accessibility bugs, design-code drift)
Does not cite made-up statistics about design system ROI or adoption
